lead: AI continues to reshape industries, prompting discussions on its implications for human judgment, safety, and societal impact.

stories.title: Why judgment matters more, not less, in the AI era
stories.summary: In the evolving landscape of AI, companies like Ford are realizing the importance of human judgment alongside automation. Despite heavy investment in AI technologies for quality control, Ford had to reinstate experienced engineers to ensure product standards. This trend highlights the necessity of integrating human expertise with AI capabilities to achieve successful outcomes.

stories.title: Sam Altman tells Politico the world “should accept some harm from AI”
stories.summary: OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman argues that the benefits of AI outweigh the potential harms, advocating for its openness to the public. His remarks reflect a growing sentiment in the tech community about balancing innovation with ethical considerations, emphasizing the need for responsible AI development.

stories.title: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
stories.summary: Despite widespread criticism of AI technologies, their adoption continues to rise. This paradox highlights a complex relationship where users express disdain for AI's implications yet remain reliant on its capabilities. The discussion raises questions about the future of AI in society and its acceptance amidst growing concerns.

stories.title: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind
stories.summary: As the AI sector expands, women are increasingly underrepresented in high-paying roles, often relegated to positions vulnerable to automation. This disparity raises concerns about gender equality in tech and the long-term implications of AI on workforce dynamics.

stories.title: Businesses are using AI to predict what individual customers will pay – and workers will accept being paid
stories.summary: Companies are leveraging AI to analyze consumer behavior and set pricing strategies, potentially manipulating perceptions of value. This trend not only raises ethical questions about transparency but also highlights the growing influence of AI in economic decision-making.

stories.title: Internet Watch Foundation reports huge rise in AI child sexual abuse material
stories.summary: The Internet Watch Foundation has reported a staggering increase in AI-generated child sexual abuse material, with assessments up 40% from the previous year. This alarming trend underscores the urgent need for robust measures to combat the misuse of AI technologies in harmful ways.

stories.title: Can ‘super intelligence’ and a non-binding safety pact solve AI’s image problem?
stories.summary: Discussions around AI safety are intensifying, with proposals for a non-binding safety pact emerging as a potential solution to mitigate risks associated with superintelligence. This reflects a broader effort to address public concerns and ensure responsible AI development.

stories.title: Trump names intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new White House AI czar
stories.summary: President Trump has appointed Jay Clayton as the new White House AI czar, emphasizing the administration's focus on AI as a transformative force. This move signals a heightened governmental interest in regulating and overseeing AI technologies amid ongoing debates about their implications.
